title: Quenching the Holy Spirit
definition: Quenching the Holy Spirit is resisting or suppressing the Spirit's work, especially His work through truth, holiness, prayer, worship, and faithful ministry.
summary: Believers are warned not to suppress the Spirit's work among God's people.
christFocus: Jesus sends the Spirit to empower, sanctify, and guide His people, and they must not resist His work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
To quench the Spirit is to suppress His work like putting out a flame. This may happen through unbelief, fear, sin, despising truth, resisting conviction, or refusing faithful service.

The warning not to quench the Spirit is joined with testing everything and holding fast to what is good.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Churches and believers can become spiritually dull through fear, sin, control, or neglect. This doctrine matters because God's people must remain responsive to His holy work.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not ignore conviction or despise faithful ministry. Test everything by Scripture, hold fast to what is good, and obey the Spirit's work through the Word.
